verdictSummary: Milanote's solo core is compact: build a local-first visual project boards app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on polish, sync, importers.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local-first visual project boards app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
whyPeopleStillPay: Milanote: People pay for a writing surface they trust for years, plus migration tools, sync, and tiny interaction details that disappear into habit.
ongoingBurden: Own schema migrations, backups, sync conflicts, export compatibility, and long-term file readability.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Local-first open-source workspace with documents and databases.

priorArt.name: Logseq
priorArt.desc: Open-source local knowledge graph and outliner.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Creative boards, documents and collections in one app, with local files underneath.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.engines: Self-hosted AFFiNE AI can be configured with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and FAL credentials
facts.dataFormat: Local-first clients keep workspace data locally and sync to AFFiNE Cloud or the operator's server; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and persistent blob storage
facts.gapVsPaid: AFFiNE's canvas is less visually refined and template-rich for moodboards, creative references, and client-ready project presentation than Milanote.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted/desktop app installs cleanly; self-hosting is a multi-service Docker deployment that needs a domain, TLS, secrets, storage, backups, and AI-provider keys for AI features

alternatives.name: Apple Freeform
alternatives.desc: A bottomless Apple whiteboard for notes, links and files; databases missed the meeting.

facts.install: Built into supported Apple devices or installed from Apple's App Store
facts.dataFormat: Boards live on the Apple device and, when iCloud sync is enabled, in the user's iCloud account; boards can be exported as PDF
facts.gapVsPaid: Freeform lacks Milanote's structured columns, task lists, project templates, board organization, and browser-accessible creative workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: An iPhone, iPad, or Mac is required, and real-time collaboration requires Apple Account/iCloud access

alternatives.name: Obsidian
alternatives.desc: Visual canvases tied to real notes and tasks, though taste is supplied separately.

facts.dataFormat: Each vault is an ordinary folder of Markdown files plus local attachments and configuration; optional paid Obsidian Sync stores end-to-end-encrypted replicas in Obsidian's service
facts.gapVsPaid: Obsidian Canvas has weaker media-board presentation, templating, card organization, and real-time collaboration than Milanote's purpose-built creative boards.

notes: Strong page because Milanote separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Milanote.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local-first visual project boards app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: conflict-safe multi-device sync; mature importers and exporters; collaborative editing and sharing.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
